sections.section_title: Paul's Opening Claim and the High Priest's Response
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes Paul's opening claim of a clear conscience before God and the high priest Ananias's order to strike him on the mouth.
The neutral reading presents Paul's sharp response to the high priest, calling him a whitewashed wall and accusing him of judging according to the Law while himself violating it.

sections.section_title: Paul and the Office of High Priest
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes Paul's acknowledgment that he did not know the man was the high priest, citing the Torah prohibition against speaking evil of a ruler of the people.

The neutral reading describes Paul's strategic declaration that he is on trial concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead, which divided the Sanhedrin between Pharisees and Sadducees and effectively shifted the dispute from Paul's specific case to an intra-Jewish theological debate.
The neutral reading describes the tribune's intervention to extract Paul from the Sanhedrin by force as the dispute became violent.

The neutral reading describes the Lord standing by Paul in the night and declaring that just as Paul has testified about Jesus in Jerusalem, so he must also testify in Rome, providing divine assurance of Paul's mission and survival.
The neutral reading describes the oath-bound conspiracy of more than forty men who vowed neither to eat nor drink until they had killed Paul, with the cooperation of the chief priests and elders.
The neutral reading describes how Paul's nephew learned of the conspiracy, reported it to Paul, and then to the tribune, who instructed the young man to tell no one.

The neutral reading describes the tribune's deployment of a massive military escort -- two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen -- to transfer Paul to Governor Felix in Caesarea.

The neutral reading presents the tribune Claudius Lysias's letter to Felix, which describes the circumstances of Paul's arrest, his Roman citizenship, the religious nature of the charges, and the assassination plot.

The neutral reading describes Paul's transfer to Caesarea under military escort, his presentation to Felix, and Felix's decision to hear the case when the accusers arrive, with Paul held in Herod's praetorium.
